description: Replace the hand-placed constructor with a multi-start SLSQP optimizer that seeds 13 random circles in the left half, mirrors them across x=0.5 to get 26, then optimizes all centers and radii without symmetry, repairs radii for exact validity, and returns the best of up to 12 seeds under a time guard.

Replace the random mirror-symmetric start with a hex-like row lattice (row patterns 5-6-5-6-4, 6-5-6-5-4, 5-5-6-5-5 cycled by seed), add small Gaussian noise, and keep the SLSQP polish and best-of-seeds selection.

Recompute final radii for each optimized center set with an exact LP (maximize sum r subject to pair and border limits), safety-clamp with _repair, then subtract 1e-12 so the packing is strictly valid.
Replace the row-lattice start in _pack_once with concentric-ring initialisation (cycling through 1/6/12/7-style ring-count variants by seed) before the existing jitter and SLSQP polish.

Replace the mirror-symmetric ring start in _pack_once with uniform random centers in [0.05,0.95] and radii 0.05 (seeded by rng(seed), seed=0 first), and run the multi-start SLSQP loop on a wall-clock budget of about 200 s using time.time().

Adds a remove-and-reinsert stage: after a short multi-start, repeatedly move the smallest circle into the largest empty hole (grid search), re-polish with SLSQP, and keep the result only if the sum of radii improves.
Edge-biased random starts: 40% of centers are sampled within 0.1 of a random border side and the rest in the interior, with the initial radius set to 0.08, before the same multi-start SLSQP polish.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement: no file or network access and no pasted coordinates.

The shrink margin drops from 1e-9 to 1e-13 relative. That is still above double-precision rounding (about 1e-14 absolute on radii around 0.1), and the run produced a valid packing. But it is close to the limit and gains at most about 3e-9 of sum, so it is not worth the crash risk.

The second SLSQP result is accepted on a larger sum without checking that it satisfies the constraints. The shrink step afterwards keeps the packing valid, but after the shrink the larger sum may not hold.

Candidate -2.6302 vs incumbent -2.6302 with one run each: the rounded values differ by 0 and there is no spread to use, so z cannot be recomputed. The reported z = 0.002 is negligible either way, and reject is consistent with the numbers.

description: Adds a second SLSQP pass from the first optimum with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter=2000, keeps it only if its repaired sum of radii is larger, and tightens the final radius shrink margin to 1e-13. This is a minimal version of the spec: it omits the explicit Newton KKT solve over active contacts.

Seed each SLSQP start with 4 corner circles, 4 edge-midpoint circles, and 18 jittered interior staggered-grid centers, so every multi-start seed gives a different structured-plus-random initial packing.

After the multi-start SLSQP loop, polish the best packing with scipy trust-constr (NonlinearConstraint with analytic Jacobian, default BFGS Hessian), keep the trust-constr result only if its repaired sum of radii beats the SLSQP result, and shorten the multi-start cutoff to 180 s for time margin.

Adds a delete-and-grow phase after the multi-start SLSQP: remove one of the three smallest circles from the best 26-circle packing, re-optimise the 25 remaining, insert a circle at the largest clearance hole, re-optimise to 26, and keep the result if it improves the sum, using a generic-n SLSQP helper and a 120 s multi-start budget.

Add a time-capped scipy differential_evolution stage over the 52 center coordinates, scored by an LP that maximizes the sum of radii for each candidate layout, then feed its best centers as an extra SLSQP start in the multi-start loop.

Before the SLSQP polish in _pack_once, run an annealed quadratic-penalty stage (mu = 10 to 1e5, L-BFGS-B over centers and radii) from each random start and feed its result to SLSQP as the starting point.

Before the penalty and SLSQP stages in each multi-start, run 300 steps of a soft-disk repulsion relaxation with radii growing from 0 to 0.09, clipping centers to the square, so SLSQP starts from a better-spread layout.

Top-k restart pool: run many cheap SLSQP starts (maxiter 100) within about 130 s, keep the 10 best seeds by sum of radii, then rerun those seeds with the long SLSQP (maxiter 1000, ftol 1e-12) and return the best.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. description: Replace the hand-placed base/interior start with random sequential placement of 26 disks whose radii follow the prescribed mixture (4x0.12, 12x0.10, 10x0.07, shuffled), use those radii as the SLSQP initial radii, and keep the existing soft-disk relaxation and penalty/SLSQP polish.

Skip the proposed "SLSQP joint optimize centers+radii" edit: train.py already runs SLSQP over joint [x, y, r] variables with analytic Jacobians, squared pair constraints, and bounds, and it already uses ring-based starts.

Before the full-space penalty and SLSQP stages in each multi-start, optimize under a diagonal-symmetry constraint (13 mirrored pairs, 39 reduced variables via a linear map, reusing the penalty function) and then release symmetry by warm-starting the existing full pipeline from that result; this is a per-start release rather than a top-5 release across starts.

Adds a seeded swap-size local search after the multi-start: swap the centers of two circles with differing radii, re-run the penalty+SLSQP polish from that start via an optional init argument to _pack_once, and accept only strict improvements, with the multi-start cut to 150 s to leave time.

Adds a staged radius-growth schedule to the penalty stage in _pack_once: radii start at 0.02 and the lower bound on each radius is raised in steps (0.02, 0.04, 0.06, then free) while mu is annealed, before the unchanged SLSQP polish.

Adds an iterated local search after the multi-start: perturb the best centers with seeded Gaussian noise cycling sigma through {0.02, 0.05, 0.1}, re-run the penalty and SLSQP polish from that start, and keep the result only if the radius sum improves, with the multi-start window shortened to 140 s so the ILS runs until 210 s.

Skipped the decaying-noise iterated local search: it repeats slot 19's perturb-and-reoptimize loop, which gained nothing, and fitting it in the time budget would cut the multi-start that produced most of the gains.

Replace the hand-placed base and interior start in _pack_once with a 5x5 grid of centers (spacing 0.2) plus one extra circle in the interstice at (0.2, 0.2), with odd-row x-shifts on odd seeds for hex-like distortion, then keep the existing relaxation and SLSQP pipeline.

issues: Integrity: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and no use of hidden labels. The crossover only recombines packings the script computed itself during the same run.

Correctness: there is no bug that makes the result meaningless. Seed 0 always runs, so pool[0] always exists. Crossover children pass through the same _pack_once pipeline, including clipping, SLSQP and whatever final radius shrink the incumbent already does, so validity is still checked the same way. Children are padded or trimmed to exactly 26 circles.
Minor: crossover can put two centres at nearly the same point, and children no longer get the mirror-symmetric init. This can only make some starts worse; it cannot make the result invalid.

Reproducibility: switching from random starts to crossover at 120 s, and stopping at 200 s, both depend on the clock. The number of jobs and which pool members get bred therefore vary with machine speed, so results are not exactly repeatable even with fixed seeds. The incumbent already stopped on the clock, so this is not new in kind.
Time budget: unchanged (stops at 200 s plus one last job), so it stays within the ~4 min margin.

Numbers: candidate -2.636 against incumbent -2.6360, one run each. The difference is 0, so z = 0, and the variance cannot be estimated from n=1 per arm. No improvement is shown, so the provisional reject is consistent. The 2.636 is above the best-known 2.635 only because of 3-decimal rounding; the harness's validity check is what counts.

description: Keep a top-5 pool of distinct multi-start packings and, after 120 s, breed children by splicing a half-plane of one parent with the complementary half of another (dropping smallest circles or adding random ones to reach 26), then relax, penalty and SLSQP polish, replacing the worst pool member when the child is better.

Replace the hand-placed base and interior start in _pack_once with uniform random centers refined by 5-15 power-diagram Lloyd iterations on a 100x100 grid (random per-circle weights), then keep the existing _relax, penalty and SLSQP stages.
Restrict the SLSQP stage to a neighbor list of pairs with gap below 0.15, run it in up to 4 rounds of 150 iterations with the list recomputed each round, and stop early once no pair is violated.
Abort: the proposed vectorised constraint caching is already in train.py, since cons and cons_jac use precomputed triu_indices pairs and fancy-index dense Jacobian filling.

Adds a seeded, time-capped simulated annealing stage over the best multi-start centers, moving one circle at a time with a decaying Gaussian step and recomputing radii by an LP (linprog/HiGHS) at each step, keeping the best packing; the final SLSQP polish is omitted to keep the edit minimal.

For odd seeds, override the base/interior start with a hex-like row lattice (row counts from three patterns summing to 26, optionally transposed, evenly spaced in [0.08, 0.92], jittered by 0.015) before the unchanged relax/penalty/SLSQP pipeline.

Abort the remove-smallest-and-reinsert-in-largest-hole idea: slot 5 already tested this remove-and-reinsert stage and it was harmful (+0.0210), and the spec's extra 60 s loop would push total wall time past the 4-minute margin given the existing 200 s multi-start budget.
Abort: pool crossover by spatial half-splitting is a near-duplicate of slot 21 (top-5 pool with breeding after 120 s), which gave zero gain, and slot 14 (top-k restart pool) also gave zero gain.

A sum of 2.636 is about 2.6359 rounded, which matches the best known result. Rounded to three places it also prints just above the 2.635 quoted in the card. That is consistent with the known optimum and does not suggest a measurement problem.

Near-active-pair constraints only: restrict SLSQP pair constraints to center distance < 0.5 with iterative re-check, to speed up restarts.

Replace the quadratic penalty continuation in _pack_once with a log-barrier continuation: start from the soft-disk centers with radii halved to strictly feasible values, minimize -sum(r) - t*sum(log slack) with L-BFGS for t = 1e-2 to 1e-5 (rejecting infeasible steps), then pass the result to SLSQP.
Aborted: per-circle soft-disk target radii were already tested in slot 29 (lognormal weights, sigma 0.35) with a delta of +0.0000, so this near-duplicate is not worth a slot.

Two-population quadrant crossover over a top-6 pool of packings, aborted without an edit.

Screen about 150 cheap starts (150-step relax, 3-mu penalty at maxiter 100, SLSQP maxiter 80) within 100 s, then fully refine (original 300-step relax, 5-mu penalty, SLSQP maxiter 500) the top 8 distinct candidates until 200 s, returning the best valid packing.

Abort: C2 (180-degree rotation) symmetric starts with a reduced 39-variable SLSQP stage, judged a near-duplicate of the already-rejected diagonal-mirror symmetric start from slot 26.

Anneal the penalty-stage objective from -sum(r^0.7) up to -sum(r^1.0) across the mu stages (log-barrier radius objective), keeping the final SLSQP on the true sum of radii.

issues: Integrity: no problems found. The diff only adds an L1 overlap penalty, lam*sum(ov), to the penalty objective, with lam stepping down 0.5 → 0.1 → 0 as mu grows. It does not read files, paste coordinates or use any external data.

Correctness: no bug that would make the result meaningless. The added gradient term, lam*(ov>0), is the correct subgradient of lam*sum(ov) as long as ov is clipped at zero (max(...,0)), as the hinge style of the nearby bl/br/bb/bt terms suggests. The ov line itself is not in the diff, so I couldn't confirm the clipping. Setting lam to 0 at high mu means the final solve is the same as the incumbent's, so validity still depends on the existing final shrink and checks.

Numbers: the candidate's loss (-2.631) is about 0.005 higher, so worse, than the incumbent's (-2.6360), and reject is the right call. The incumbent's 2.6360 is just above the card's rounded best known 2.635, but the best known value is about 2.6358, so this is consistent after rounding.

z: I can't recompute it exactly. Each side has only one run, so there is no sample variance. The reported z ≈ -3554 roughly matches a difference of 0.005 divided by a noise SD near 1e-6 (0.005/(1e-6*√2) ≈ -3536). The gap is probably from rounding of the adjusted values. Whatever the exact z, the direction and the decision hold.
